NEW DELHI: Looking to further expand their strategic partnership, India and Poland agreed to double bilateral trade by 2030 and announced dialogue mechanisms for defence industrial collaboration and counterterrorism cooperation as PM Narendra Modi hosted his counterpart Donald Tusk for talks Thursday.Modi and Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.Poland views the war in Ukraine as a direct threat to its national security and sovereignty due to its shared border, influx of refugees and the threat of future Russian aggression in eastern Europe.“They reiterated the need for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in line with international law, consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity,” said the joint statement. The leaders also noted the negative impacts of the war on global food and energy security, especially for the Global South.Modi and Tusk, the first Polish PM to visit India in 16 years, also backed an MoU under negotiation for cooperation in critical minerals.Modi said the friendship between India and Poland was based not only on diplomatic ties but also on a shared heritage of humanity and empathy. He recalled how, during the Second World War, the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter in India to thousands of Polish children and families. He also thanked Poland for helping India evacuate Indian students from Ukraine shortly after the Russia-Ukraine war began in 2022.Modi said the world was passing through a period of uncertainty and change, and even in such times, both India and Poland were emerging as important hubs of growth, technology and innovation.“Today we have agreed to deepen ties in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India,” he said.He also announced a startup bridge to facilitate cooperation in IT, Artificial Intelligence and critical technologies.“Both India and Poland believe in democratic values and the rule of law,” Modi said, underlining that both sides considered reforms essential to make global governance institutions more empowered.The two countries agreed that the UN needed structural reforms, including expansion of UNSC in both permanent and non-permanent categories, to remain relevant, credible and effective. In the joint statement, Poland expressed support for India’s membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC, as well as its candidature for a non-permanent seat on the council for 2028-29.Modi and Tusk unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, and stressed that there could be no justification for terrorism on any grounds.“They condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in J&K’s Pahalgam on 22 April, 2025. They called for strong and concerted action against terrorists and terrorist entities, including those designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee,” said the joint statement.Defence and security cooperation was a major focus, with the leaders underlining importance of an Agreement on Mutual Protection and Exchange of Classified Information and expressing expectation it would be signed soon.They proposed a defence industry dialogue to develop a “forward-looking framework for defence industrial cooperation”, including business-to-business engagement and, where mutually agreed, partnerships in technology, co-development, co-production and other forms of collaboration.
Article Summary: Poland views the war in Ukraine as a direct threat to its national security and sovereignty. PM Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace. Both sides considered reforms essential to make global governance institutions more empowered.

NEW DELHI: The Cabinet Secretariat did not take any action on complaints filed by two election commissioners against an officer in the Election Commission, saying the letters were written in their “individual capacity” and did not represent the poll panel as a whole, according to documents released in response to an RTI application.Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had separately written to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29, raising concerns about the conduct of senior deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg, an IAS officer appointed to the Commission by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) on September 2, 2024.The letters were provided in an RTI response to activist Commodore Lokesh K Batra (retd).The Indian Express had reported in September that the two Election Commissioners approached the Cabinet Secretary after Garg issued a work allocation order that they believed could concentrate powers over changes to voter records at the central level, instead of allowing officials at the state level to handle them.In a statement on September 26, the Election Commission said the work allocation orders issued by Garg were never implemented following directions from the two Commissioners.The poll panel also said the complaints concerned an officer on deputation and not matters related to policy or the IT division.According to a Cabinet note included in the RTI response, both Commissioners alleged that Garg had issued an order changing the work allocation of officers senior or equivalent to him after taking charge as the link officer of the deputy election commissioner (Administration).The Commissioners said the changes were made without consulting the Commission or the officers concerned. They also alleged that Garg acted despite repeated oral and written instructions against making such changes without prior discussion or approval from the Commission."Both the ECs have stated that Shri Garg, after assuming the charge as link officer of DEC (Admn), has issued an order regarding work allocation of equivalent and senior officers to him without discussing the revised work allocation with the Commission or the officers concerned. Further, the aforementioned ECs have stated that this has happened despite repeated oral and written instructions to all concerned officers against taking such actions without prior discussion/approval of the Commission," the Cabinet note said.The two Commissioners alleged that Garg's actions violated the chief election commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.Joshi also said that when he sought the relevant file from the Administration Division, it was not provided to him.A Cabinet note prepared on August 3 proposed seeking the chief election commissioner's opinion on the complaints."In this connection, we may request the chief election commissioner for his opinion on the issue. Accordingly, a draft DO is put up for approval, please."However, a subsequent note dated August 4 said taking action on complaints from individual Election Commissioners without an official communication from the Commission as a whole could be seen as interference in the functioning of the constitutional body."The Commission is a Constitutional Body and is insulated from executive interference by design to ensure that it functions independently and in a transparent manner. The working and functioning of the Commission are governed by the rules and guidelines of the Election Commission. The above communications are from the Election Commissioners in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the Commission as a whole," the note said.It added that although Garg had been appointed by the ACC, he was now an officer of the Election Commission, and his work and conduct were governed by the poll panel's rules and guidelines.The note also referred to Section 18 of the 2023 Act, which states that the Commission should conduct its business unanimously as far as possible, with any differences of opinion settled by a majority decision."Election Commissioners have sent these communications for appropriate action; however, in the absence of any official communication from the Commission as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate. It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the Constitutional Body. Hence, it would be appropriate to send acknowledgement to both Election Commissioners with a copy to PPS to CEC for information of CEC," the note said.The draft note signed by Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan was also marked to the secretary of the department of personnel and training and the establishment officer to keep the matter on record.The note said this would "enable it to be taken into account in future decision-making regarding the officer".Somanathan also signed an acknowledgement letter confirming receipt of the complaints and sent copies to both election commissioners.The letters were acknowledged on August 5, 2026, with copies marked to the department of personnel and training, the Establishment Officer and the office of the chief election commissioner.
Article Summary: Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had separately written to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29. They had raised concerns about the conduct of senior deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg. The Cabinet Secretariat did not take any action on complaints filed by two election commissioners against an officer.

NEW DELHI: Amid SC’s scrutiny of hospitals charging patients steep mark-ups on medicines and consumables, govt officials have flagged gaps in data and regulatory hurdles in extending price controls to hospital supplies, saying the Centre first needs to establish the extent of margins before considering intervention.The Union govt has told the SC in its affidavit that margins on hospital consumables can range from 100% to 1,000% or more, highlighting concerns over the high mark-ups patients often face on supplies used during treatment. However, a senior official told TOI that the govt does not have the data needed to assess margins across hospital supplies and determine whether wider controls are warranted.“We first need to get the data and then examine whether there is a margin and a need to control it,” another senior official said, explaining that the purchase price of medicines and consumables would need to be compared with what hospitals charge patients before deciding on any intervention.Centre fixes ceiling prices for scheduled medicines and has limited annual price increases for non-scheduled drugs up to 10%. It has decided to cap trade margins on certain anti-cancer medicines at 30% of MRP. Extending similar controls to other medicines and hospital consumables, officials said, would require analysis and consultation.A health ministry official, however, raised doubts about how far the govt could regulate hospital billing, saying hospitals, with health being a state subject and governed by the Clinical Establishments Act or other laws enacted by state govts..The Centre’s role, the official said, is largely confined to drug-price regulation through the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority.Regulating individual components of hospital bills would be difficult, the official said, pointing out that hospitals charge package rates without providing detailed itemised bills. Restricting charges on consumables could lead profitconscious hospitals to raise other fees, including surgeons’ charges, the official argued.The official also disputed the blanket use of the term “overcharging” when hospitals bill patients at the MRP, saying there is no general legal requirement to offer discounts below the printed price. They cited delayed reimbursements from insurance firms and govt health schemes as financial pressures on hospitals that would need to be factored in while deciding any broader intervention.

Article Title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Supreme Court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

As cases of estranged NRI couples fighting for child custody increasingly result in cross-border litigation, with one spouse getting a favourable order from a foreign court while the other moves an Indian court, Supreme Court has said courts here must make an independent assessment of what is good for the child and the ruling of the foreign court should not be automatically followed, though it must be accorded proper consideration.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child “must be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort alone”.“This position rests on two foundations. The first is that once the court is seized of the matter, it exercises its parens patriae jurisdiction. That jurisdiction obliges it to consider and assess the matter for itself, through the lens of the child’s welfare. The second is that the decision in such cases turns not on the legal rights of the parties but on the welfare of the child. The same emphasis on welfare over legal entitlement runs through our statutes on custody and guardianship. They make clear that a person otherwise entitled to custody or guardianship need not be granted it if that would not be for the welfare of the child.There is thus no ambiguity in the fact that an order of a foreign court must yield to the welfare of the child,” the bench said.“Put differently, a court in this country, when exercising its jurisdiction, cannot blindly follow the order of a foreign court and act merely as an executing court,” the apex court bench said.SC said a parent’s disobedience of a foreign court order did not, by itself, require the Indian court to give automatic effect to that order and also that the paramountcy of the child’s welfare did not mean that the order of the foreign court had to be disregarded. “In deciding what the welfare of the child requires, the court must form its own independent judgement. In doing so, however, it must give proper weight to the order of the foreign court,” the bench said.SC passed the order while directing that a seven-year-old girl, a US citizen, who was brought to India by her mother in breach of a California custody order, return to US.A California court had in 2022 granted the couple joint custody of the child and specifically barred her removal from California without written consent or a court order. In violation of the ruling, the mother left for India with the child after two weeks, leading to the father starting legal proceedings against her in India.SC allowed the petition of the father, who approached the court through advocate Prabhjit Jauhar, against a Karnataka HC order dismissing his plea. After hearing both sides, it said the welfare of the child lay in her continuing to reside in US.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said courts here must make an independent assessment of what is good for the child. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again.

JAMMU: A Jammu court has imposed two life sentences and fines of Rs 2 lakh on Mohammed Sharief, a terrorist who gunned down three members of a family, including a six-month-old infant, in Ramban district’s Gool area over 21 years ago.In his order on Wednesday, principal sessions judge Ramban Ajay Kumar Gupta rejected defence arguments that the attack had taken place more than two decades ago when Sharief was young, his long incarceration and possibility of rehabilitation.Besides the life sentences, the court imposed two separate terms of 10 years on Sharief under various sections pertaining to murder and arms act offences. “All sentences shall run concurrently, while the period already spent in custody shall be set off in accordance with law,” the judge said.The court ordered that the fines be paid to those injured in the July 2005 terror attack and directed J&K State Legal Services Authority to provide compensation to heirs of the deceased and the survivors.Judge Gupta rejected defence arguments about the testimony of two injured eyewitnesses, saying they were reliable and corroborated by medical and other evidence. Defective investigations or delay in recording statements could not automatically result in acquittal when credible evidence otherwise established the accused’s guilt beyond reasonable doubt, the judge said.Public prosecutor Wajid Ahmed pressed for maximum punishment under law, contending that the murder of three innocent family members, including the baby, and the use of an AK-47 rifle warranted a stringent sentence.The court considered aggravating and mitigating circumstances and held that although the crime was extremely grave, the case did not warrant the death penalty under the rarest of rare principle.

Article Title: New norms to limit fuel leaks, protect EV batteries in rear-end crashes
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Govt has tightened norms for protection of fuel systems and electric power drive systems, with all new vehicles manufactured from April 2029 onwards required to comply with the new standards, a move that will prevent fire in rear-end collisions.In a notification, road transport ministry has also made the automotive standard, AIS-192, mandatory for Event Data Recorder (EDR) from Oct 2029 if it is installed in any car. The EDR feature is not mandatory for all cars, and it remains an optional feature. EDR records crash details, which help establish what happened immediately before and during a collision. It is similar in purpose to an aircraft’s flight-data recorder or black box.In the case of standards for fire safety, the revised automotive industry standards (AIS)-101 specify that after a rear-impact crash test, liquid-fuel systems must not develop more than slight leakage and continuous leakage must not exceed 30 grams per minute. The key safety requirements include the fuel system not allowing a fire to be sustained following the impact. In the case of electric vehicles, the battery and its securing mechanism must remain in position during and after the impact test.This standard lays down requirements for protecting occupants from electrical hazards, including the high-voltage circuit being automatically disconnected after a collision.The ministry has notified revised vehicle safety standards, including updated frontal and side-impact crash protection requirements, with implementation for new models scheduled from Oct 2027 and for all models from Oct 2028.It has also revised requirements for protecting pedestrians and other vulnerable road users. The updated standard will apply to new models from Oct 2028.
Article Summary: Govt has tightened norms for protection of fuel systems and electric power drive systems. All new vehicles manufactured from April 2029 onwards required to comply with new standards. Move will prevent fire in rear-end collisions. Road transport ministry has also made the automotive standard, AIS-192, mandatory.

Article Title: Natco’s generic SMA drug approved; ‘clinical trial’ labels trigger Kerala row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Days after a controversy erupted in Kerala over Natco Pharma’s generic drug for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), regulatory clarifications suggest the row stemmed from labels on bottles supplied free of cost. The words “Physician Sample/Clinical Trial” raised fears among parents that their children were being given medicines meant for clinical trials rather than an authorised drug for routine treatment.In response to queries from TOI, Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) officials said Natco’s risdiplam powder for oral solution (0.75 mg/ml) had been approved by the Telangana State Food and Drug Administration under the applicable regulations. The bulk drug had received CDSCO approval on April 7, 2025.The officials said bioequivalence studies were not required for the oral solution under the regulator’s draft guidance and that additional clinical trials were not necessary before patients could be switched to the generic formulation.Natco said it emerged as the lowest bidder in Kerala’s tender and supplies one free bottle for every three purchased under its Patient Assistance Programme, bringing the effective cost to around ₹8,500 per bottle against ₹1.5 lakh earlier for Roche’s drug.The company acknowledged that the free bottles carry the label “Physician Sample/Clinical trials only”, but said they were supplied as samples under the rate contract and not for clinical trials. It said its generic risdiplam, priced at an MRP of ₹15,900 against ₹6 lakh for Roche’s product, had met regulatory requirements.The issue became a political controversy after Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said parents of children with SMA had flagged the labels on medicines distributed through SAT Hospital in Thiruvananthapuram. He alleged violations of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules and procurement norms and demanded an inquiry.SAT Hospital authorities have maintained that the medicine distributed was the approved generic formulation, not an experimental drug.Risdiplam is used to treat SMA, a rare genetic disorder that causes progressive muscle weakness. Kerala had been supplying Roche’s branded medicine free to eligible children at a negotiated price. The shift to Natco’s generic version could substantially reduce treatment costs and potentially allow the state to extend support to more patients.The controversy comes amid opposition from parents and the Cure SMA Foundation of India to Kerala’s decision to replace Roche’s medicine with Natco’s generic version. Parents have sought assurances about the safety and efficacy of switching children who have improved on the existing treatment.While the regulatory clarification addresses the generic drug’s approval status, the episode raises a separate question: whether labelling that combines “Physician Sample” and “Clinical Trial” can cause confusion when medicines are supplied for patient use.
Article Summary: Regulatory clarifications suggest the row stemmed from labels on bottles supplied free of cost. The words “Physician Sample/Clinical Trial” raised fears among parents. Natco’s risdiplam powder for oral solution (0.75 mg/ml) had been approved by Telangana State Food and Drug Administration.
